I do not recommend this funeral home. My experience was awful almost a year ago.
At the worst possible time after my father's death, the person who attended to us lacked empathy. They reluctantly made memorial cards with photos. They told us it wasn't customary to include photos, which shocked me. The photo I provided was included at a distorted size, and his face was completely disfigured. I had to return the cards, and they had to remake them all. The casket, under the pretext that it was "eco-friendly" and had "eco-friendly varnish," was full of imperfections. I had to ask them to move my father to a casket without defects. And yes, it looks like an airport, but in the room where they put my father, there was a leak right above the coffin.
Everything couldn't have been worse. At the worst moment of your life, when you lose a loved one, the last thing you want to do is complain. I believe that funeral services are expensive enough without the treatment, professionals, and materials need to be of the highest quality.

one_star_reviews.text:
I visited this clinic for a dermatology consultation. My appointment was scheduled for 18:45, and I arrived 10 minutes early.
I was not informed that the doctor was running behind schedule and ended up waiting until 19:30 to be seen.

During the consultation, Dr Reguero asked only very basic questions before requesting that I undress to examine my skin condition. The blinds were open to a busy street and I expressed my discomfort. I was told, “Don’t worry, no one can see you,” I felt uncomfortable throughout the examination.

Dr Reguero diagnosed me with a relatively rare condition and advised me to research it online. I was prescribed a cream, and the entire consultation lasted less than 15 minutes. I was charged €120.

I was then booked for a follow-up appointment two months later. I assumed that the follow-up would either be included in the initial fee or at least offered at a reduced cost. However, I was informed that it would cost another €120. When I raised concerns about my experience and the level of service I had received, the response was simply: “Do you want to cancel?”
I felt disappointed by the communication. As a foreign patient, I had specifically asked in advance whether the doctor spoke English, as I felt it would be easier to explain my concerns. I was reassured that she did, yet the entire 10 mins consultation was conducted in Spanish.

Overall, I found the experience unprofessional and lacking in patient care. Given the lengthy wait, the brief consultation, the handling of my concerns, and the pricing structure, I cannot recommend this clinic.

one_star_reviews.text:
I do not recommend this company. Extremely careless handling of belongings, and if anything gets damaged, it seems impossible to get the company to take responsibility.

We shipped a suitcase and several boxes from Spain to Romania. When they arrived, the suitcase was damaged and dirty. The boxes arrived in terrible condition: torn along the seams and sides, dented, and damaged. They even managed to tear a vacuum cleaner box made of very thick cardboard and break a sturdy plastic hanger inside it. It was obvious that the hanger had caught on something outside the box, tearing the cardboard from the outside and breaking the hanger. Some other items sustained minor damage, and one small item never arrived at all - it may have fallen out through a hole in one of the boxes. Almost all the smaller cardboard boxes packed inside the larger box were also crushed.

However, the biggest problem was a cosmetology chair that had been packed in one of the boxes.

Before transport, the chair was practically new, fully functional, and stable. It moved easily and smoothly on its wheels. After transport, it wobbles, and one of the wheels no longer touches the floor, leaving a gap of approximately 0.5-1 cm. As a result, instead of rolling smoothly in the intended direction, they turn sideways, catch, and drag across the floor. The chair is difficult to move, has lost its stability, and no longer functions properly. In its current condition, I cannot use it safely.

I contacted the company to resolve the issue. First, I sent an email, but received no response for a week. I then contacted them via WhatsApp. They replied that the company was not responsible because the items had already been delivered and should have been inspected at the time of delivery. After I sent another message, they simply ignored me and have not responded since.

This raises an obvious question: how exactly was I supposed to inspect 120 kg of belongings in the middle of the street? Was the driver expected to wait while I unpacked every box, checked every item, and tested the chair? How could I properly test the chair on uneven asphalt? How was I supposed to test electrical equipment outside without a power outlet? And what if it was raining? The driver did not even offer us the opportunity to inspect the belongings - he simply unloaded everything and quickly drove away.

What is particularly frustrating is that the problem with the chair was not visible during a routine visual inspection. It only became apparent when I tried to use it. The absence of obvious impact marks does not mean that an item could not have been damaged during transport.

I move frequently and have used various transport companies. With other companies, the boxes usually arrived in almost the same condition in which they had been sent. This time, I handed over intact boxes and received them torn and crushed. This was not just damage to fragile items, but also damage to things that should have been able to withstand normal transportation.

Unfortunately, I did not photograph every box upon delivery because I had no intention of filing a complaint. I only have one photo, which was taken for another purpose.

So if something gets damaged, the company may simply point out that you did not inspect everything at the moment of delivery and refuse to address the problem.

I do not recommend this company if you want your belongings to be handled with care and expect the company to at least try to find a solution if something is damaged.

We also had another unpleasant experience: we were told to carry 120 kg of belongings downstairs because the driver wouldn’t wait, but in the end, our belongings weren’t collected. We were left with all the boxes outside and no elevator to carry them back up. Moreover, we had to empty the apartment within two days before flying abroad, so it was essential to have our belongings collected that day. Yet the company made no effort to help us find a solution. We had to figure everything out ourselves. I’ll write a separate review about this incident.

one_star_reviews.text:
I left my book on consignment at this bookstore about a year ago, and the experience has been disappointing.

Of all the copies I gave them, only two were sold. The rest ended up in storage, and several people who came specifically to buy it told me they were told there were no more copies left, even though the books were still there. I don't know if it was negligence or a lack of interest, but the result is the same: lost sales of a book that was physically in the store.

On top of that, they wanted to keep a percentage of the profit, much higher than what other bookstores had offered me for the same type of arrangement.

I understand that a book on consignment isn't a business's priority, but if you agree to the arrangement, the least you can do is properly inform anyone who asks about it. I expected better service, especially from a Christian bookstore. I wouldn't return, nor would I recommend it to other authors.

one_star_reviews.text:
After-sales service or just a way to make the customer pay?

My experience with this company has been utterly disappointing, and frankly, it's hard to understand how they can consider their warranty management acceptable.

The air conditioning compressor in my Mercedes broke down after only 5 months. Instead of taking responsibility or providing a technical explanation for why the breakdown was excluded from the warranty, the solution was very simple: make the customer pay for the entire part.

The reason?

An expert report that, according to the information they provided me, doesn't actually determine the cause of the breakdown.

Instead of offering a clear technical conclusion, the report mentions things that "could" have caused the breakage: worn pulleys, a dirty condenser, faulty fans, etc.

In other words: they don't know—or can't prove—what caused the breakdown, but they do know perfectly well who's going to pay for it: the customer.

And this is where it's hard not to feel cheated as a consumer.

Because when a company charges for a part that fails after five months and, to avoid taking responsibility, uses a report that suggests possibilities instead of demonstrating a specific cause, the impression it conveys is very clear: they're looking for any possible explanation to avoid honoring the warranty and pass the cost on to the customer.

If there really is a cause that excludes the warranty, why isn't it conclusively proven?

Why isn't it demonstrated that this was the actual cause of the failure?

Why are hypotheticals presented as "it could be" and then used to justify making the consumer pay?

This doesn't convey transparency or trust. It conveys a way of operating where the objective seems to be avoiding costs for the company, even if it means the customer has to bear them.

I didn't expect such a crucial vehicle part to fail after five months, but I certainly didn't expect that, faced with such a premature breakdown, the response would basically be to find excuses and present the bill to the consumer.

Getting paid is easy. Demonstrating the true cause of a breakdown and taking responsibility when necessary is what shows a company's seriousness.

In this case, my experience has been exactly the opposite.

I feel wronged and deeply disappointed by how the warranty was handled. And after this experience, I would never trust this company again, nor would I recommend it to anyone without thinking twice.

When a company is more interested in finding an excuse to avoid paying than in technically demonstrating what happened, the customer inevitably ends up wondering if they are dealing with genuine after-sales service or simply a system perfectly designed to make the customer pay.

A disgraceful management.

This morning I went with my three children (9 years old, 2 years old, and a baby) to buy items for an event.
While we were browsing, my 9-year-old daughter picked up a loose display balloon, and when she did, the string came undone. I fully understand that she shouldn't have touched it, and I have no problem with her being told off for it.
What I found completely inappropriate was the way the salesperson spoke to her, scolding her for what had happened, and then continued talking to me, telling me to keep a closer eye on my children.
It's one thing to correct a child, but quite another to do it in a way that makes a family who's simply come in to shop feel uncomfortable. Furthermore, in a party supply store, where many items are displayed and specifically aimed at children, I think it should be taken into account that a child might accidentally touch something, and that there are much more polite ways to handle such situations.
We left without buying anything at all because of the way we were treated. It's a shame, because we would have definitely bought something there and probably returned another time. Of course, after this experience, I can't recommend the establishment.
I went this morning with my three children, in case the establishment wants to be aware of the situation.
Thanks for nothing.

Last week I requested information about a postgraduate course. The website said there were scholarships available (they're direct discounts, not scholarships). As soon as I entered my information, a salesperson contacted me via WhatsApp. He was very insistent from the start that I enroll. These courses cost around 2,000 euros, so it's not like buying a loaf of bread. He immediately told me how lucky I was to have a scholarship, but that I only had three days to apply. Yesterday, Sunday, October 11th, at exactly 5:21 PM (I repeat, Sunday), he told me that the deadline was approaching. Obviously, I didn't reply. This morning, October 12th, a national holiday, they wrote to me again at 10:15 AM, this time much more curtly, saying "Scholarship rejected." I replied that they could respect my Sunday and weekend hours for contacting me via personal WhatsApp, without knowing their condition... and the conversation, to put it mildly, turned bizarre... to the point where they asked if I was a psychologist, questioning my qualifications... I ended up having to block them because they wouldn't stop replying, even after I politely asked them to stop... but they didn't care.

I recommend that this person's boss let them rest on holidays because otherwise, you end up with salespeople harassing clients to sign them up for courses because they're under pressure to sell...

Obviously, NB Psychology is out of the question for any training... if they treat clients like this, what can we expect from their courses?

My experience at this official Toyota dealership was very negative. The receptionist, Belén, didn't seem to have the necessary training to deal with the public, and her service left much to be desired.

Furthermore, the mechanics offered contradictory diagnoses. They also assured me they had carried out a two-day test drive, but when I checked the MyToyota app, I saw that the car hadn't been moved during that time. This lack of honesty makes me extremely distrustful. I've been to other official Toyota dealerships on the Iberian Peninsula, and the difference in service is enormous.

If you decide to take your car there, I advise you to have the mileage recorded when you drop it off, demand a detailed and stamped invoice, and verify that the work listed matches what was actually done. In my case, I prefer to take the car to the mainland rather than return to this establishment, even though it means more time and expense. It's regrettable that it has to come to this for a brand like Toyota.

one_star_reviews.text:
I went there twice, first they confirmed a time, the day before they called me and told me a different time, I said it wasn't the time they told me and they treated me like a liar, I went at the time they said, they kept me waiting for more than an hour in the waiting room. In 5 minutes I was out without knowing what I had.
Next visit, more than an hour again in the waiting room to cover a cavity in a wisdom tooth, although before I asked if they were okay or if there was any problem. He said everything was perfect, he covered the cavity in 5 minutes without even saying a word to me, he was constantly going in and out of the room to go with other patients, half a year later 3 nights without sleeping and today another dentist confirmed that they have to pull out the tooth that covered me.
Very bad service, very bad attention and I feel scammed for charging me to cover a cavity in a tooth that should not have been covered but pulled out, apart from the fact that he told me that I had 5 more cavities to cover when today they told me that I only have 1 to cover.
Total disappointment.

Since I could not answer your answer or make a new one, I complement it, I came in December to have a cleaning and check the gums. My last cavity was taken by my father to cover it when I was 10 years old, I had not had much oral care for MANY years and I admit it. Even so, you told me that I had 5 cavities to cover, at €65 each, the price of the mutual insurance, €325, the thing is, today, half a year later, after a second check-up, new x-rays and opinions from 2 dentists, I only have 1 cavity to cover.
Besides, they told me that I have to pull out my wisdom tooth on the top left, curiously, it has a filling. How funny that my last cavity was covered when I was quite young and I didn't have wisdom teeth yet but this one is covered.
Finally, as I see other people commenting, patients are people, treat them as such, not like bags of money, the relationship with the patient is important and that in 2 visits I spent more than 3 hours in the consultation, but that the effective time was a maximum of 30 minutes between cleaning and cavities, while you were going from room to room, leaves a lot to be desired from a health professional

one_star_reviews.text: I am deeply sorry to post this review, but the string of errors and lack of professionalism from the funeral home has been a complete disaster. At such a difficult time, having to argue about each and every service contracted and paid for well over 50 years with an exemplary company, this funeral home has managed to ruin every single service. Flowers, catering, customer service—not to mention the cleanliness and condition of the facilities. It truly couldn't have gone worse. The only positive thing to mention is the excellent service from the reception staff, both the night and morning shifts. These poor women are the face of the business and the ones who bear the brunt of the damage, even though they are not at fault. They went out of their way to try and rectify every single mistake. Thank you both. Otherwise, you should seriously consider relinquishing management and letting professionals do the job. Those of us who have to come here, unfortunately, don't do so by choice, and the experience is made much less bearable by unprofessionals like yourselves.

Terrible experience at this funeral home. I attended a funeral yesterday, and all the common areas lacked air conditioning. With extremely high temperatures and in the middle of a heatwave, the facility failed to meet the basic health and safety standards required of this type of establishment. Every public center must comply with minimum habitability and thermal comfort standards to avoid risks to attendees and staff. We were informed by the center itself that this situation was recurring.
I hope Mémora takes the appropriate measures.
The air conditioning isn't working, the heat is unbearable.

What's going on with the air conditioning in the building? It seems to be the same old problem. August 18th, with an outside temperature of 38 or 39 degrees Celsius, and only air conditioning in the rooms; the central hall and the chapel are like ovens. People are trying to cope with the heat using fans. Stifling and shameful. Coslada should aspire to better.

one_star_reviews.text:
Forklift Operator Course: Terrible Management, Faulty Accreditation, and Incorrect Information

I completed the theoretical and practical forklift operator course on May 8th. After finishing the course, the overall experience revealed significant shortcomings in several operational and management aspects that I feel are important to point out:

Lack of Rigorous Training and Evaluation: The practical sessions were completely incomplete. The theoretical exam is a mere charade, lacking validity and transparency; no one informs you of your grade, and there are no clear evaluation criteria, with everyone passing as a formality.

Delays and Missed Deadlines: They promised to deliver the license in two weeks, but it took more than two months. After having to go there several times to no avail and receiving constant excuses, customer service proved to be nonexistent.

Deplorable License Quality: The license issued is simply a piece of cardboard covered with poor-quality plastic. The printing is so poor that the letters rub off at the slightest touch, and the design contains duplicate text fragments clearly copied and pasted.

Serious errors in the documentation: On the issued diploma, although my name was correct, they included someone else's ID number. The document was also riddled with strange symbols and formatting errors, demonstrating that they don't even verify the information before sending the emails.

A highly unprofessional company. I do not recommend taking their course if you are looking for serious training and a proper certificate.

one_star_reviews.text: Good afternoon, I just came from the Día supermarket on Extremadura Street in Fuenlabrada. The sign says it's open until 8 PM on Sundays. I arrived there at 7:40 PM and they were already locked in. They refused to open the door. A Black man came out saying it was closed, that it was closed, that it wasn't going to open. There were three of us at the door, telling him there was a sign on the door saying it was open until 8 PM, but he insisted it was closed, that it was closed, and went back inside and pulled the shutter down in our faces. He wouldn't let us in. There was a woman with a small child there too. We should have called the police; I thought of that too late, but what a disgrace that businesses advertise opening hours and then close whenever they feel like it. We're going to report this on Telemadrid.

I'm giving it one star because I can't give it less. We've been without an elevator for over two months, waiting for a part, and all we get are excuses. Disabled people can't even leave their homes. I'm waiting for the manager to call me, but I'm already sitting down. INCOMPETENT.

The manager never called me. They've already come to fix the elevator, and it's broken down again twice.
We had to file a complaint to get them to come and remove the mess they left in the building entrance. It'll probably take them another three months to come and take it away.

0 stars. If you hire this company, you'll be climbing stairs a lot. Last month the elevator stopped working, supposedly because of a part we had to wait for. When it was finally installed, the elevator only worked for 15 minutes. They finally repaired it, but two weeks later the elevator is out of service again. Here we are waiting for a security guard who's supposed to come before 7:00 PM. Let's hope for the best.

one_star_reviews.text: Good morning, I haven't felt up to writing reviews, but I'm doing so now because two months have passed since it happened. My daughter sadly passed away on July 28th, and her cremation was at 12:30 AM on July 29th. Everything was fine until the person responsible for removing the flowers opened the door and told her friends that she was going to proceed and that there were some relatives nearby. At that moment, they called her father, uncle, and me as her mother. This woman had already lowered the curtain and closed the door. We knocked and asked her, and she rudely replied that she had already notified them. Our response was that it's normal to tell her parents, not her friends—something simple and easy to understand. One should always empathize with the family, and in my opinion, this woman didn't. Any case is sad, but the loss of a young girl breaks your heart into a thousand pieces. I hope that this woman will be taught some proper way to treat people.

The dishes they told us they had weren't actually there; we had to order different ones, and when they arrived, they were cold, as if they'd been taken straight from the refrigerator. It took almost 50 minutes for the food to arrive. When we asked the staff several times for coffee and to pay, they were scrambling to see who would do it, with sour faces, slowness, and reluctance. Honestly, I would never eat here again. It's a shame that at a time of loss, when all you want is to spend those last moments peacefully with your loved one, you have such terrible service. And it's not just the customer service that's bad; they treat each other badly too, with curt responses, indifference, and so on. Their organization is also appalling, with everyone blaming each other for not putting the order on the computer, asking where the orders were, whether they'd been paid yet, or claiming they didn't know. Everyone is just wandering around the place without any clear roles. In short, I'm speechless.

one_star_reviews.text:
The truth is, I'm quite disappointed with Anarela's organization. It's one thing for the occasional unexpected event to come up, but it's quite another for appointment changes, staff changes, and a general lack of organization to be so commonplace. In the end, it's the patients who have to constantly adapt and worry about whether our appointment is still scheduled or who will be seeing us.

I also wanted to specifically mention the reception staff, because I think it's something they should review. The woman who usually works at reception often chats with her colleagues about her personal life, listens to personal audio messages, and engages in conversations that, frankly, I don't think are appropriate when you're dealing with the public. And I'm not just saying this because of the impression it gives, but because I've needed to go to reception a few times and there was no one there to help me.

I find it quite frustrating that these things happen and that it seems like no one notices or that they've simply become normalized.

And now, on top of everything else, they're asking for prepayment. I completely understand that a center can set its own payment terms, but if patients are required to pay upfront, I think it's also reasonable to expect much better organization, communication, and care.

I believe they should listen more to complaints and seriously review how things are being done, because from the outside, there appears to be considerable disorganization and a lack of professionalism in some aspects.

one_star_reviews.text: A complete disappointment, I'm very upset. This hair salon, with so many years of experience and a fantastic reputation—which I imagine took them years of hard work to build—can't live off past glories from over 20 years ago. Prestige, professionalism, and a good reputation are earned daily, with the same effort and enthusiasm, because times change, trends change, and of course, clients change. It's business 101 that it's easier to lose a client than to gain one. Here, that doesn't seem to matter much. I was looking for what they advertise so heavily on their website: "We have qualified professionals who will advise you on the care of your image, your hair, and your skin."... "Latest trends in cuts and color. We advise you on defining your style and on the care of your hair."... "Our philosophy is to create personalized styles for each client, with the expertise of traditional hairdressing and the latest innovations and trends."... Well, I can assure you that I FOUND NONE OF THAT. What I got was a haircut from a neighborhood barber. But what disappointed me most, when I complained, was that they didn't even tell me to come in so they could see it or how it could be fixed. Now I'm walking bad publicity for that company because when people ask me who did it, I have to tell the truth. And another sign of their lack of professionalism: they should be just as fair in the morning as in the afternoon, which apparently doesn't exist in the afternoon. Some people have already given all they have to give to the company, and if they don't keep up with the times, they should consider retiring and making way for new generations. I'M SO, SO, SO DISAPPOINTED THAT I WON'T BE BACK. IT'S NOTHING LIKE IT'S ADVERTISED ON THE WEBSITE.

I decided to stop those treatments and work with my primary care physician to find the best option. It's incredibly expensive, they don't provide follow-up care, and they don't offer support during periods of negative thoughts... In short: they're just trying to rip you off.

one_star_reviews.text:
Gross negligence, unethical behavior, and irreparable harm. A danger in the courts.
Run. From the very beginning, they exuded a worrying air of charlatanism, but what happened in court crossed every ethical and legal boundary.
I hired the forensic expert to conduct a clinical trauma assessment. Anyone who has been through something like this knows it's an incredibly difficult process, requiring complete vulnerability and profound revictimization so that the damage is properly documented. It demands an extreme level of rigor and respect for the patient.
The result of his work? After putting me through this psychological ordeal and collecting his fees, he appeared in court in such a severe state of cognitive impairment that he ended up confessing to the judge that he suffered from Alzheimer's. Everything was recorded in the official courtroom audio.
The most scandalous and negligent aspect is the cover-up by his wife, Dora Estrada. She knew perfectly well that he was unfit to practice or even set foot in a courtroom. However, instead of acting ethically and removing him from the case, she offered to accompany him to court to "assist" him in ratifying the report, despite being a clinical psychologist, not a forensic one. In the end, her husband appeared alone, since ratifications are exclusively by one person, and he made us look ridiculous with a disorganized, guru-like speech, explaining nothing and completely undermining his scientific credibility, constantly rambling and visibly irritating the judge.
Accepting a clinical and legal assignment of this magnitude while concealing his state of health is not only unjustifiable professional negligence; it is an absolute lack of humanity. His reckless incompetence undermined my defense, caused me financial hardship by being ordered to pay court costs due to his mental incapacity, and has caused me, above all, devastating emotional damage by forcing me to relive a trauma for absolutely nothing and shattering my trust in the protection systems.

A series of negligent acts that should result in his disqualification. Utterly deplorable.

one_star_reviews.text:
Well, my first experience at this hair salon couldn't have been worse. I went yesterday morning for a cut and style. I showed the stylist, Merche, the cut I wanted (I'll attach all the photos). While she was cutting the back, everything was fine, but the front didn't look like it was going to turn out as I'd shown her. But in the end, she's the professional, and you trust her. She styled it, and the back did look good with that style. I went home, and looking in the mirror, I saw something I didn't like... Imagine my surprise when I decided to wash my hair... and I had a cut that was absolutely not what I asked for. But the worst part is that it's completely unusable. I asked for a bob with the front below my jawline, and it ended up at my cheekbone. The cut isn't straight, nor is it even slightly shorter in the back, which is how a bob should be. Merche told me that in the photo I'm showing, the girl has textured ends, which is perfect because I love it that way, but... she went overboard with the texturizing and completely ruined the cut. I religiously paid the 39 euros to wash, cut, and style hair that was already short; it didn't even come close to my shoulders. I pay because her work is done, badly done, but done, and I'll never refuse to pay. But I absolutely do not recommend this hair salon, and obviously, I won't be going back. Now I'm stuck wearing my hair up with 20474929 bobby pins until it grows back and someone can fix the mess.

Best regards.

I'm editing the review to add that the day after I wrote it, Merche contacted me to tell me to come down to have my cut checked and fixed. I couldn't make it that day, and the next morning Arantxa, I think she's the owner of the Venus salons, contacted me. Merche apologized, and again urged me to come down and see it, at least, since they weren't happy to hear I was upset about the haircut. So, I went down yesterday at 4:00 PM. Merche, as always, was very kind and made a real effort to convince me to let her fix it. I have to admit I was terrified of cutting any more hair, but I trusted her, and now I'm very happy with my cut. I want to take this opportunity to thank them for contacting me after my review and for going to the trouble and taking the time to fix it so I was happy. I'll definitely be back. Things like this don't always happen. Thank you, Merche and Arantxa.

one_star_reviews.text: I went on August 7th for a neck strain and left with a damaged nerve due to improper handling, writhing in pain and unable to sleep. I went to the ER three times and to a rehabilitation specialist once. They all agree it was improper handling that damaged my nerve. I'm taking pregabalin and Enamplus, but they haven't taken responsibility for my recovery, knowing the injury was their fault. Of course, I'm not saying they didn't try to relieve my pain in good faith, but we're all human and sometimes we make mistakes unintentionally. But out of professional ethics, they should have taken responsibility for something they caused, even unintentionally. They moved my last appointment from 8:30 PM to 7:00 PM, and after waiting 40 minutes, I had to leave. It's true they called to apologize, but that doesn't make up for my lost time, which is also valuable, by the way! I had to go to the emergency room that same night because I couldn't stand the pain anymore. My arm was so swollen it was burning hot. In the end, I'm the one who has to endure the pain, the sleepless nights, and on top of that, pay for everything out of my own pocket to try and fix what they caused in a physiotherapy session for a simple muscle strain. It was just a minor discomfort, but it wasn't keeping me up at night or causing these awful nights and days I'm having. I wouldn't wish this on anyone. I honestly expected them, as professionals, to take responsibility for their negligence, but they didn't. Anyway, I hope no one has to go through what I'm going through, and who knows how long it will last. By the way, I even have to pay for an MRI out of my own pocket, as if I were responsible for what's happening to me. All I can do now is wait for the MRI and hope the rehabilitation specialist can fix what your clinic caused.

If you have the opportunity to explore other options, do so. They only pay attention to you until you make the payment, and then you cease to exist for them. They sold me a bill of goods about obtaining a professional certificate in Extremadura for ambulance transport, which doesn't exist. I've asked them for help repeatedly, but I'm practically invisible to them now. Honestly, I feel completely scammed. I absolutely do not recommend them.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving it a 1 because I can't give it less.

I'm going to share my experience because I think it's important for other people to know before leaving their car here.

I left my car for a total of 5 days. First of all, I want to warn you about something important: the locations shown on Google indicating where the parking lot is are NOT REAL.

I was shocked when I went to pick up my car and saw that it had 27 km more on the odometer than when I left it. When I asked about this discrepancy, the first explanation they gave me was that they might have recorded the mileage incorrectly when I picked it up. Coincidentally, I have photos that prove the mileage.

I spoke with two guys, and neither of them could give me a coherent explanation for why my car had 27 km more on the odometer. They told me that one of the parking lots was very close and that the other was about 10 km away. When I asked them for the exact location of the parking lot so I could check the mileage myself—which, by the way, still didn't add up—the most surreal thing happened:

THEY TOLD ME THEY COULDN'T TELL ME WHERE MY CAR HAD BEEN FOR 5 DAYS BECAUSE THE LOCATION WAS “SECRET.”

Excuse me?

We're talking about my car, which I left in their care for 5 days, and they can't tell me where it was parked. The parking lot's address isn't on any of the paperwork, contracts, or documents I signed.

I find this incredibly unprofessional and completely unacceptable.

And there's another detail that strikes me as even more odd. When I complained about the mileage, they told me that perhaps they had recorded it incorrectly. According to them, the information was given verbally and they didn't verify it at the time. I have photos of the mileage, so that explanation doesn't seem valid to me.

Furthermore, from the very first call when I complained, they told me that perhaps the mileage had been "given incorrectly." Considering the number of vehicles they receive, it's quite difficult to believe they could remember exactly what mileage was verbally reported to them days before.

Frankly, the 27 km discrepancy, the lack of a clear explanation, and, above all, their refusal to tell me where my car has been for 5 days, claiming the location is "secret," is very worrying.

I can't say what was done with my vehicle during those kilometers because I don't have that information. But it's precisely this lack of transparency that makes me distrustful.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wanted to print some invitations on onion skin paper. When I entered the shop, I explained that I wanted to print the PDF I had prepared in A5 format and that, if they had suitable envelopes for the invitations, I also wanted to buy them.

From the moment I mentioned that I wanted to use onion skin paper, the saleswoman's reaction was not good. Even so, she went to cut the paper and, when she returned, brought sheets in A4 format. At first, I thought that perhaps she was going to print them that way and then cut them, but upon checking, I realized that she was preparing the print job in A4, when I had specifically brought the document in A5.

When I pointed out that I had asked for A5, she insisted that this was not the case and even told me that she "never paid attention to formats." When I tried to explain what I had requested, she started tearing the paper rudely and speaking to me in a way that I consider completely inappropriate, calling me "sweetheart" and "love" in a clearly sarcastic tone.

Faced with the situation, I told her I would pay for the photocopies I had already made, even though they were A4, but that she shouldn't make any more because her behavior was making me uncomfortable and I wanted to leave. Despite this, she continued yelling at me and kept preparing more tracing paper to make A5 copies. I asked her to stop, and then she reprimanded me, asking what she was going to do with the tracing paper, since, according to her, she wasn't using it for anything.

The situation made me very nervous, and to try to end the conflict, I told her to only print those sheets and not the rest. I insisted again that I wanted to pay. At that point, she started calling me "girl" in a derogatory way.

I asked her if another employee could please help me because the situation between us was becoming very uncomfortable. Her response was to yell at me: "I'M THE BOSS!" At no point had I questioned who was in charge of the store. I was simply asking for someone else to help me because I wanted to pay and leave.

Later, other customers came in, and she served them before me, leaving me waiting. When they finished and left, she said, "If you're feeling more relaxed, I'll print them for you." I replied no, that she should just charge me. The situation escalated again, and since I couldn't stand the tension anymore, I headed for the door. What's even more surreal is that, at that point, she wasn't even making it easy for me to pay and leave.

Once at the door, I explained that the PDF was prepared in A5 format and that I had done my part correctly by bringing the document in the format I wanted. I believe that if there was any doubt about the requested format, the normal thing for a professional to do would have been to ask me and confirm it before printing.

I'm self-employed, and I know perfectly well what it takes to run a business. That's precisely why I insisted on paying, even for prints that weren't the ones I had requested. But there's a difference between a mistake or a misunderstanding and the way a customer is treated.

I left the store in tears and with an overwhelming sense of helplessness. I won't be back, and of course, I cannot recommend this establishment. If I ultimately take further action regarding this incident, it will be because I consider the treatment I received to be absolutely unacceptable.

one_star_reviews.text:
I took my car to the garage for a service, air conditioning repair, and to fix a problem with a screw. Before they started the work, I asked for an estimate, but they never provided it and, without notifying me or asking for my authorization, they carried out the repairs. The final cost was around €400.

The most worrying thing happened the day after I picked up the car. While I was driving, the "possible engine failure" warning light came on. I was completely stunned and, above all, scared, because you take your car to a garage precisely expecting to leave with it in better condition and safer.

I called the garage, and they told me to come in because, according to them, it could be a false alarm. When I arrived, however, they told me it wasn't a false alarm and that I had to leave the car there.

The next day, I called to ask if the problem was covered by the warranty, which I thought was logical considering the warning light had appeared practically the day after they worked on it. To my surprise, they told me that since they "hadn't checked the engine," the problem wasn't related to the work they had done and that I would have to pay for it myself.

Naturally, I went to pick up the car the next day.

I find this situation highly unprofessional: I requested an estimate, which they didn't provide, they carried out work without informing me of the cost beforehand, and then, the day after I picked up the car, a serious warning light appeared related to the engine.

I can't say exactly what happened, but the coincidence is, at the very least, very worrying. I'm now without a car and €400 poorer, and the garage hasn't offered any solution.

A very unpleasant experience, and certainly not a garage I would return to or recommend.

one_star_reviews.text:
You're greeted with the elegance of a headless chicken running in circles. You walk in, say what you need, and the hipster friend (a creature clearly designed by the Hate for Joy Committee) looks at you as if you've been prescribed plutonium.

Every time you ask for the brand-name medication, he offers you the generic with the conviction of a preacher in the throes of an epiphany. You insist, he insists. It's an epic, yet sad, duel, like two snails colliding in slow motion. It's a reminder that life doesn't always offer expensive wine and interesting conversations.

You leave with the feeling of having survived a religious experience, but a bad one, the kind that leaves you questioning your life choices.

Oh! And on top of that, it's expensive.

one_star_reviews.text:
I can't assess her skills as a psychologist because, ultimately, I didn't even get to have the session. What I can assess is how she manages appointments, and my experience has been very negative.

I booked an appointment for a Friday, and the policy stated that payment was to be made via Bizum 48 hours in advance. Due to an oversight, I hadn't yet made the payment by Wednesday. At 10:06 PM, I received a direct message informing me that, since payment hadn't been received, the appointment was canceled. There was no prior reminder, no question of whether I was still interested, and no option to make the payment at that moment.

I completely understand that there are rules and that a professional wants to protect their schedule from cancellations, but I also believe that, especially when working with people who may be seeking help precisely because of stress, anxiety, work overload, or difficult personal situations, one would expect a minimum of empathy and flexibility in communication.

I also find it quite unprofessional that the booking system depends on the patient remembering to manually make a Bizum payment. Today, there are payment gateways and automated systems that allow you to collect payment upon booking, send reminders, or notify you before canceling an appointment.

In my case, being automatically canceled two days prior, via a message sent at 10 p.m. without offering any alternative, struck me as a rigid and patient-centered approach.

After this experience, I will certainly be looking for another professional.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience at this clinic was quite disappointing, especially considering the consultation cost €110.

I went mainly hoping to see my baby and find out if it was a boy or a girl. I also mentioned that I'd like a printed copy of the ultrasound to keep as a memento. However, during the appointment, they barely tried to get a suitable image to print, and the quality of the ultrasound I finally received was quite poor.

What bothered me most, though, was the way I was treated. I'm a heavier woman, and I fully understand that this can make an ultrasound technically more difficult. What I don't find appropriate is the way certain comments were made about my weight, nor the feeling that they were in a hurry to finish the appointment.

I had ultrasounds during this same pregnancy at the public healthcare system, and with the equipment and conditions they had there, my baby was perfectly visible and very clear. That's why I was surprised that during this appointment they insisted so much that the image wasn't clear because of my weight, without me perceiving any real effort to get better images.

I understand that an ultrasound can have limitations and that a perfect image isn't always possible. What I expected, especially paying €110, was a more personal, respectful, and patient experience, and that they would try to make the most of the appointment so I could take home a nice keepsake of my baby.

I left quite disappointed, not so much because of the image quality itself, but because of the way I felt treated at a moment that was especially important to me.

I went for a 3D ultrasound. The receptionist was very unpleasant throughout the entire appointment, even while filling out my form, and she was very rude. The gynecologist was nicer, but she only gave me a brief examination and didn't provide any report, just telling us the baby's weight. She couldn't perform the ultrasound because of the baby's position, and on the way out, the secretary charged us €110 for the consultation. As I said, it was a half-hearted consultation with no report. We left there completely bewildered.

one_star_reviews.text:
I contacted this center to schedule an adult autism spectrum disorder (ASD) assessment. They explained the process and told me the total cost was €500, but that I had to pay €250 upfront before any in-person appointments.

I asked if I could pay at the first appointment or in installments, since the process has distinct phases (questionnaires, interview, tests, report). They told me that wasn't possible and that full payment had to be made before starting.

I also asked what would happen if the diagnosis wasn't confirmed at the first appointment, and I didn't get a clear answer about a refund.

I understand that each center has its own policy, but in my case, paying €250 without an in-person appointment or meeting the team made me feel uneasy. I prefer centers that allow payment in installments or at the end of the process.

If you don't mind paying upfront, this might work for you. But if you're looking for transparency and flexibility, I recommend exploring other options.

one_star_reviews.text: I find it appalling that someone so unpleasant and rude works in customer service. I used to go to this pharmacy a lot, but I won't be setting foot in it again after the rude way I was treated by a blonde pharmacist with glasses. She didn't even say good morning, she spoke to me with such arrogance and superiority as if everyone else were an idiot. Not even an apology or goodbye, she just left me there without a word. Seeing the other negative reviews, it seems this isn't an isolated incident.

I'm giving it fewer stars because I can't. My experience with this gynecologist was terrible and, frankly, a disgrace considering the price of a private consultation.

From the very beginning, the treatment was extremely unprofessional. He wouldn't look me in the eye when I was speaking, the appointment was incredibly quick, and I constantly felt like he was eager to finish so the next patient could come in. I felt like he just wanted to get me out of there as quickly as possible, without listening to me or giving me the necessary time.

But the worst part is the reason I went to the appointment. I went mainly for an ultrasound because I have a lump in my breast. During the examination, because of how quickly he was doing everything, he didn't even examine the lump. I had to ask him if he had looked at it, and his response was that he had forgotten. He then had to repeat the ultrasound to check.

And, to top it all off, the diagnosis he gave me doesn't match at all the diagnosis I later received from the public healthcare system. I find it particularly serious that, by paying for a private consultation precisely seeking more careful attention, the result is such poor care and a diagnosis that has later been contradicted by another professional.

Alternator in my Fiat Ducato wasn’t charging the battery. Mechanic said that they’ll investigate it. After 4-5 hours he informed me that car was fixed. When I came to pick up my car he said that they had to replace the alternator and the total cost is over 1000 euros 🤯 He didn’t ask if I want to buy the alternator for around 700 euro net, he just changed it. And what’s more, the battery still wasn’t charging properly. I had to return to the mechanic and it took another day to find out that the issue was with the ground cable. I made to pay for it additionally. And at the end it turned out that the alternator wasn’t broken 😡
Please avoid this place if you need, specially when you’re a tourist.

one_star_reviews.text:
We purchased four stands from Guil in February 2024 for professional touring and theatre work, and unfortunately our experience has become increasingly disappointing over time.

The stands fall apart from regular use, we have encountered repeated and serious reliability issues, including:

• Wire ropes repeatedly coming off pulley wheels
• Damaged pulley wheels and cable failures
• Faulty safety catches, including one that did not work from delivery
• Handle grub screws constantly loosening
• Magnetic locking pins breaking and coming loose
• Cheap plastic wheels making the stands unstable and difficult to move safely

Most concerning is that one of the original winches was clearly faulty from the start. After replacing the winches ourselves, the stands worked, confirming the originals were defective. Had we followed the advice initially given to us instead of replacing them, it could potentially have resulted in a serious safety incident.

Most recently, during a theatre show on Sunday night, another cable came off the pulley wheel while lowering a stand. Due to the poor accessibility of the pulley system, it was impossible to repair onsite, and after nearly two hours we had no option but to cut the cable just to safely lower the stand and load it into the truck.

We take excellent care of all our equipment and operate in professional theatre and event environments where health and safety standards are critical. These stands are still within the advertised 36-month warranty period, yet we were charged over €700 for replacement winches that we strongly believe should have been covered under warranty.

Another frustration for UK customers is that Guil will not ship replacement goods directly to England, meaning you are forced to arrange and pay for your own courier collection, adding further inconvenience and expense when already dealing with faulty equipment.

What is equally disappointing is the apparent unwillingness to take constructive criticism onboard to improve the products. We raised genuine concerns regarding safety, reliability, and servicing access, particularly around the pulley system design, yet there seems to be very little interest in addressing these issues properly.

At this stage, we are seriously considering returning all four stands and requesting either full replacements or a refund.

Very disappointing experience for equipment marketed as professional touring products.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving him one star because I can't give him less.

My experience with this lawyer has been, without exaggeration, one of the most unpleasant I've ever had with a professional.

I went to him expecting to find someone who would at least listen to my situation, inform me of the actions taken, and treat me with the minimum respect that any client deserves. What I found was exactly the opposite. From the very first moment, his behavior was marked by arrogance, condescension, and a way of speaking to me that made me feel constantly belittled.

During our conversations, I encountered phrases and responses unbecoming of a professional entrusted with defending someone else's interests. Far from offering clear explanations, he adopted a permanent attitude of superiority, as if asking questions about my own case were a nuisance or an act of intrusion. Expressions like, "What do you think, that I'm your servant?" "Don't think you have so many rights in life just because you're disabled"... That was the general tone of our conversations.

What was most worrying was the feeling of abandonment. After agreeing that she would submit a written statement to the court informing them of my disability and vulnerability, I asked if she had actually done so. It was a simple question that required a simple answer: yes or no. However, far from answering, she began asking questions about other matters and diverting the conversation. To this day, I still don't have the clarity I should have received from the very beginning.

As a person with a recognized disability of 67%, it was especially painful to witness the lack of sensitivity shown toward a circumstance that directly affects my legal and personal situation. I wasn't expecting preferential treatment; I expected something much more basic: respect, consideration, and professionalism. However, I felt that my circumstances were met with indifference, if not outright disdain.

The fact that she hung up on me twice pretty much sums up the level of consideration I received. He claims he never hung up on me, the call simply dropped. But when you're having a conversation with someone and the phone line cuts out due to lack of signal, the simplest rules of courtesy dictate that you call back, which he never did.

There are professionals who honor the legal profession with their training, their education, and their respect for others. My experience with this lawyer leads me to conclude that, unfortunately, he is not one of them.

I would not recommend Roldán to anyone expecting dignified treatment, especially if they are dealing with people with disabilities, because they will find not a shred of empathy, transparent communication, or even a minimum of human sensitivity. The feeling this experience leaves me with is that I was treated by someone deeply outdated in his manner, extraordinarily rude, and completely incapable of understanding that behind every case file there is a person who deserves respect. I certainly wouldn't recommend it 👎👎
To my surprise, one of the attempts to contact them to get an explanation—which was unsuccessful, as my written request had been submitted—only just received a response today... however, instead of replying, they expressed their desire to take me to court over this review 😨
I was "invited" not to express my experience through a public review and that, if I had any complaints, I should limit myself to contacting the Bar Association. Personally, I believe that those of us who use legal aid deserve the same respect and the same right to express our opinions as any other client.

⚠️ I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS CENTER.

I had Skinbooster and Indiba treatments. The injections were performed by Dr. Ana López.

After the treatments, blisters appeared, along with increased sensitivity, changes in skin texture, and new wrinkles, especially around my eyes. I informed the center of my symptoms and canceled my appointments.

Subsequently, I required dermatological evaluation and follow-up, both in the public and private sectors, including a clinical examination, skin ultrasound, and dermatoscopy. The dermatological evaluations I received indicated that both the Indiba and Skinbooster treatments had been applied incorrectly. I am currently continuing dermatological follow-up to treat the remaining issues.

I waited a few months to observe the progress before publishing this review.

My experience has been VERY NEGATIVE. Due to everything that happened and the subsequent dermatological follow-up I required, I DO NOT recommend going to this center.

one_star_reviews.text: It's the worst scrap yard I've ever seen. When you call, the woman asks how many kilos you're bringing, and if it's less than 20 kilos, they won't buy it. Besides that, they pay 1 euro less than other scrap yards for the cover.

I don't recommend it: the owner's arrogance and lack of professionalism.
I went to Taller Vega to get a quote for changing all four of my car's tires. The owner asked for the tire sizes and license plate number, and I specifically asked if, once he ordered them, he would call me the following week to confirm availability. He assured me that he would, that he would have them between Monday and Tuesday, and that he already had my phone number (although he hadn't asked for it at that moment).
Three weeks have passed, and they haven't even bothered to call or contact me. It seems like they don't care about the customer and that, if they have too much work, they should just say so directly instead of wasting people's time. Completely inadvisable due to the owner's arrogance and lack of professionalism. Even bigger companies have fallen; in this world, arrogance gets you nowhere.

I'm very disappointed with the club. After four years, this past season was enough to convince me to take my son out. And I know it wasn't just my experience, because several children who were there ended up switching to the same club as my son.

After four years, I'm leaving very disappointed. My son deserves a place where his effort is valued and where he's treated with respect and equality.

one_star_reviews.text:
On May 15, 2026, I placed an order for furniture from the manufacturer José Ibáñez through the Rústico Colonial website. The order consisted of a dining table, four chairs, and a sideboard.

After waiting for more than two months, the order was finally delivered on July 22, 2026. To my surprise, both the table and chairs did not match what I had ordered and paid for.

Specifically, the table was delivered in a completely different color than the one I had chosen, while the four chairs arrived upholstered in green, when the color selected in the order was beige.

I immediately contacted you, and you acknowledged the error. Given this situation, I sent the chair seats back to be reupholstered in the color I had originally selected.

However, approximately one month later, I received the seats back, and far from resolving the problem, the result is a very poor and unprofessional finish, with a quality that I consider completely unacceptable for a new product. I've attached photos so you can personally verify the condition and finish of the work done.

On the other hand, the problem with the table remains unresolved. To this day, I still have a table at home in a color that doesn't match the product I purchased at all. I believe the solution should be simple: deliver the table in the color I selected and paid for, and arrange for the collection of the incorrect table.

I was told that the collection would be arranged at the end of August. However, it's now September 5, 2026, and the collection still hasn't taken place. Furthermore, I'm being told I might have to wait another month and a half to two months to receive the correct table.

This is a completely disproportionate situation: almost four months have passed since I placed and paid for the order, and I still haven't received the products as purchased.

I wish to express my profound dissatisfaction with the handling of this order, both due to the errors made and the delay in providing a definitive solution, as well as the quality of the subsequent work.

I believe that, as a customer, I have fulfilled my obligations from the outset, including paying for the order, and it is unreasonable that I should have to bear the consequences of errors that are not my responsibility, nor continue waiting for months to receive what I originally purchased.

Therefore, I request an immediate and definitive solution, including the replacement of the table with one in the requested color and a suitable solution regarding the poor finish of the chairs.

I expect this complaint to be addressed with the seriousness and speed it deserves and that I will receive a satisfactory solution without further delay.

Unfortunately, the experience thus far has been very negative, and unless this situation is resolved appropriately, I will not trust your company again nor recommend your services.

one_star_reviews.text:
A few months ago I got my license at this driving school. The experience? Awful. Everything was fine until the practical lessons. Well, fine, I waited more than six months for my first lesson. It's true that there was some flexibility regarding the lessons and they never gave me any trouble about taking them consecutively, nor did I stop doing them, so that was great. But the instructor... a disaster. Instead of teaching you to drive, he spent his time talking about a thousand things you couldn't care less about, lecturing you nonstop. The worst part is that you pay and pay for nothing. The clutch friction point? I learned that from a TikTok driving instructor. How to get the car off a hill? Same thing, TikTok... Parking? I did it once, the day before my test. It's a disgrace. And the fact that your instructor calls you and leaves a message to grab a drink after you've passed? How unprofessional... I don't understand how the owner can hire people like that; they should have much more oversight.
Price assessment
Overpriced

one_star_reviews.text:
A very disappointing and, from my point of view, completely unprofessional experience. I do not recommend this driving school.

My experience was quite bad. On several occasions, I felt that their main objective was to get me to sign up for more lessons, rather than actually teaching me how to drive and properly preparing me for the exam.

The lessons were 45 minutes long, but often the explanations were neither clear nor sufficient. For example, when approaching an intersection, I wasn't given advance instructions on how to react, which made an already complicated situation for a learner even more difficult. I was also told to shift gears before braking, something that can be quite complex for a beginner if it isn't explained correctly and patiently.

Furthermore, when I made a mistake while braking, instead of calmly explaining how to do it correctly, the instructor told me I needed physical therapy because he was tired of being hit by those sudden stops. These kinds of comments, instead of helping me correct my mistake and learn, only made me more nervous and tense. A person who is learning needs explanations, patience, and professional feedback, not to feel guilty or pressured for making mistakes that are part of the learning process.

Another aspect that I found particularly unprofessional was that, when I had a question during the lesson about how the car worked and asked the instructor to explain something, he would sometimes tell me to look it up on his Instagram. That's precisely what an instructor is for: to teach, answer the student's questions, and make sure they understand what they're doing. If I'm paying for a lesson and I have a question, I expect to receive an explanation during that lesson, not be told to look up the answer on social media.

I was also very disappointed by the lack of preparation for the exam. I didn't feel that I was adequately taught the routes, the situations that could arise during the test, or the strategies needed to approach it safely. There were even times when music was played during the lesson when, from my point of view, what I needed was for the instructor to be focused on explaining and correcting me.

After all the time and money I invested, I left feeling like I'd wasted time, money, and, above all, my confidence behind the wheel. A driving school should help you feel increasingly confident and prepared, not leave you more nervous, confused, and frustrated after lessons.

The only positive thing I can say is that the receptionist was always very kind, understanding, and accommodating. She definitely made a good impression on me.

But as for the teaching itself and my experience with the instructor, I'm deeply disappointed. For me, a good instructor doesn't just tell you what you're doing wrong; they explain why it's wrong, how to do it correctly, and give you the tools you need to improve.

The consequence of this experience was having to find another way to learn and regain the confidence I had lost. Therefore, before investing time and money in this driving school, I recommend thinking it through very carefully and making sure the teaching method truly suits your needs.

one_star_reviews.text:
STAY WELL AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY — DO NOT BUY ANYTHING FROM THEM!

They have stolen money from us and are completely unprofessional and, in our experience, dishonest.

Our own car was falling apart, and even the AC had stopped working. In 38°C heat, we urgently needed another car. We met the salesperson, Nacho, who appeared trustworthy. He told us about his previous work for Audi and discussed which car brands were considered the best and worst. After listening to what we were looking for, he recommended a Nissan Juke that was currently being rented out. He showed us a similar Juke and told us that if we bought through them, the car would be completely refurbished and serviced — inside, outside and mechanically. We were explicitly promised, both verbally and in writing, that the car would be in perfect condition when delivered.

We paid €500 to reserve the car. Nacho said it would be ready within 2–3 weeks and that we should not pay the remaining amount until he confirmed that the matrícula was ready.

After a week, we heard nothing. When we contacted Nacho, he told us to deal with Adan instead. Eventually Adan sent us a preliminary matrícula on WhatsApp and again confirmed in writing that the car would be in perfect condition, although he could not guarantee a specific delivery date.

Weeks passed. We repeatedly asked for a collection date because we had to return to Norway, arrange insurance and sell our old car. After several delays, Adan said it would be ready in another two weeks. When we complained about the extremely poor service and said we were losing confidence in the company, he suddenly said it would be ready Monday and promised to call that morning. He never called, did not answer his phone, and nobody at the company answered. We finally reached someone on Tuesday and arranged to collect the car the following day.

When we arrived, the car was nowhere near the condition we had been promised. There were numerous unrepaired scratches, a dent inside the front-door area, chips in the windscreen, strange noises from the AC and engine, and the engine was shaking violently. During the test drive it sounded and drove like a tractor, with severe mechanical noise.

We said we could not accept the car. They offered to repair it, but we had already waited five weeks, one of us was leaving the next day, and after all the broken promises and terrible communication, we had completely lost confidence in them. They offered another car, but that would also require waiting for weeks. We cancelled the purchase.

Initially they told us there was no problem and that all our money would be returned. Then the owner/manager, Maria Prieto, said they would retain €390 for matrícula costs. Later she changed this and said they would calculate their expenses and deduct those instead.

Six days later, we received the refund — and they had wrongfully withheld €1,254 from us.

We reported them to the police. The police themselves told us that their conduct was criminal and that they considered this a scam. We have also reported the company to the relevant authorities.

On top of everything, they had arranged an insurance policy in our name without our consent, with monthly payments, and even deducted money for this.

Because of them, we also lost the opportunity to sell our old car, had to cancel insurance arrangements, spent weeks waiting for a car that was never delivered as promised, and lost considerable time and money.

They lied to us, broke their promises, treated us extremely poorly and wrongfully withheld €1,254 of our money.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY. DO NOT BUY A CAR FROM THEM.

one_star_reviews.text:
1 star is way too much to give this company!!! We bought an IMR BULL 1000W electric mini quad on December 12, 2025. It cost us €475. Unfortunately, the quad broke down quite quickly. Because the weather was very bad and we had to return to the Netherlands several times for hospital visits, our son was only able to ride it twice during that time. In April, our son wanted to ride it again, but unfortunately, the fuse kept blowing due to the switch. I contacted them immediately because, well, I assumed it couldn't suddenly break down after riding it twice!! Eventually, the quad was repaired and covered under warranty, which was another thing, because when we brought it in, they said they didn't know if it would be covered under warranty! Fortunately, they covered it under warranty, otherwise I wouldn't be done with it yet, of course!!

Our son was only able to use it for a short time, because you guessed it, BROKEN AGAIN!!!

Emailed again on July 11!! The fuse keeps blowing again and again!! The quad is kept dry and is rarely used! We are very careful with our belongings, so it really sucks that our son can't ride it whenever he wants to!! A friend was visiting us and they really wanted to ride the quad, but well, BROKEN!!! To this day, this store has not come up with a solution!! I have asked the store to get in touch so that we can return the quad and get our money back!! But of course, they aren't responding!!

I do not recommend buying anything here!! In any case, these quads are very bad, break down quickly, and the service is also very poor!! A word to the wise is enough!!!

I am VERY DISAPPOINTED with how my purchase was handled, especially the exchange.

I bought a backpack for €67 and a pencil case for €13, for a total of €80, and paid by card.

In the afternoon, I went to exchange the backpack for another one for €55. That's when they applied the two €30 school vouchers. In my opinion, the logical thing would have been to first refund the original €80 purchase to my card and then process the new transaction using the vouchers.

However, that's not what happened.

The sales assistant made a mistake and only tried to refund the €12 difference, keeping the €80 I had originally paid, plus the €60 for the school vouchers. In other words, I would have lost money unfairly.

Furthermore, I had to speak with three different people to try to resolve the situation, which only made the whole process even more frustrating and slow.

First, they tried to give me the €55 for the backpack as a gift receipt. I had to insist before they finally refunded it to my card. Then, they also gave me the remaining €12 as a gift receipt to spend in the store.

To top it all off, they told me I would lose €5 of the €60 in school vouchers because the new backpack cost €55.

I find this completely unfair and very unclear. If I paid for an €80 purchase with my card, I don't understand why, when making an exchange, I end up with a gift receipt, lose money from the school vouchers, and, on top of that, initially receive an incorrect refund.

I am very angry and disappointed with how everything was handled. I shouldn't have had to argue, insist, or explain the situation to three different people to get a correct refund for money I paid by card.

I hope they seriously review how they are handling exchanges and school vouchers because the experience was very negative.

A completely useless organization for defending property owners against negligent property managers.

I filed a formal complaint against one of its members, Ms. Ana María Rodríguez Llano (no. 27324/395) of Administraciones Corona S.L., documented and with evidence, for systematic malpractice and for expressly refusing to provide a complaint form (an incident recorded). The result: the Disciplinary Committee dismissed the complaint without any real investigation.

I filed an appeal more than 40 days ago. Zero response, zero acknowledgment of receipt, despite having formally requested it. Today they called me to verbally inform me that they will not take any action.

A professional association that protects its members instead of ensuring the quality of the service they provide serves no useful function for society. They simply collect membership fees and turn a blind eye when a citizen reports malpractice.

I've had to escalate the complaint to the Consumer Affairs Directorate of the Principality of Asturias and to the Ministry. Let this serve as a warning to other property owners: this professional association is not an effective channel for filing a complaint, and neither is Administraciones Corona S.L. as a management company.

one_star_reviews.text: About six or seven years ago, I don't remember exactly, I went for a consultation and rhinoplasty with Dr. Valdés. I chose him because he had been recommended to me as an excellent doctor (I'm referring to rhinoplasty; I'm not mentioning other surgeries because I only had this one with him). I went to him because I wasn't comfortable with my nose. The consultation was perfect. Marta was very kind, and he explained the entire process very clearly. He gave me confidence at that moment, and I was very excited about the change. The first rhinoplasty was done the "old school" way; back then, ultrasonic surgery didn't exist. I wanted to file down the septum and thin the tip. After a few weeks, the results, despite the swelling, were good. I liked some things, but on the other hand, I wasn't very happy with others. I decided to give him time. He said he couldn't do more because my skin was too thick, even though it was entirely possible to treat it and achieve a result closer to what I had initially asked for. I decided to wait, since the full results of a rhinoplasty only become visible after years. But as time passed, I realized that my upper lip was too close to my spine. He suggested a touch-up, which I paid almost €1,000 for, in addition to the nearly €5,000 I paid the first time. That second time was terrifying. It was done with local anesthesia in an operating room where it hurt a lot; I could hear and see everything. Afterward, I liked the result a little more, but it still didn't completely convince me. It was a yes, but no. During that process, my visits to his office were few and far between, and only for the first few months. After that, he forgot about me as a patient. Years later, I realize that having this surgery with him was my worst decision. My nose widened, it "grew," and a cartilage spurt appeared on the right side, which is deviating my nose to one side, looking terrible aesthetically. It's blocking that nostril, making it impossible for me to breathe properly, and the tip is even rounder than before. I still have internal stitches that never came out; they get infected, smell bad, and make it hard to blow my nose because they sometimes stick out and poke me. This has created enormous insecurity in me. Today, I'm 10 days away from traveling to Colombia to see a reconstructive surgeon who specializes only in noses, since that's what I need right now. Paying a lot more money for this procedure, and with the fear that this time it will finally work and improve both my quality of life and my self-esteem, because as a result of all this, I find it hard to take photos, smile, and feel good when I look in the mirror. He never called me again for proper follow-up after the surgery, except for the first few months, and he never bothered to check on my recovery afterward. The reason I didn't contact him again was because I already knew the damage he had done. I hope this new doctor finds what little he left me and gives back what Dr. Valdés once took from me, which was my self-confidence. I don't know what his surgeries on other parts of the body are like, but I absolutely do not recommend him. What once filled me with hope now saddens me when I see it in the mirror.

I went to this bookstore the other day to pick up some books for my daughter, and when I tried to pay with a €100 bill, they refused to accept it. The most surprising thing is that there was no sign or notice indicating that they didn't accept €100 bills.

Given this situation, I asked for a complaint form to document what had happened, and they told me they didn't have any, and they even laughed at the whole thing.

Finally, I had to leave, get change, and go back to pick up my daughter's books. When I returned with the change, they had finally printed and posted a sign indicating that they didn't accept €100 bills. In other words, when I went the first time, that notice wasn't there; it appeared after the incident.

What bothered me most, even more than them not accepting the bill, was the attitude of the person who served me, practically laughing in my face while I was trying to resolve the problem and asking for a complaint form. This situation was completely unnecessary, and the customer service was extremely unprofessional and disrespectful. I certainly won't be shopping here again.

My experience at this center has been deeply disappointing due to the lack of empathy and sensitivity towards the patient.

In particular, the psychologist Nazaret Hernández Suárez gave me the impression that she was more focused on the number of sessions and the financial aspect than on listening to, understanding, and addressing the patient's real needs. The administrative staff's behavior didn't help either: despite already having a prescription and authorization, she tried to schedule an appointment for me two months later. Far from seeking a solution, she even told me that if I didn't like or respect their rules, I could go to another center, even though I had correctly followed all the required procedures.

I consider it a real disgrace that someone seeking psychological care is treated this way. Patients are not simply sessions to be billed: we are people who need to be heard, respected, and have a minimum of empathy. I certainly cannot recommend this center.
