Disappointing experience overall. The offices are quite small and feel overpriced for what you get.

The elevator is basically a freight/service lift and, in my experience, breaks down regularly. Definitely something to consider if you’re on a higher floor.

The place also feels seriously understaffed, so getting quick support or decisions when needed can be difficult.

Noise is another major issue. People regularly take phone calls in the corridors, and meetings/conferences are sometimes held with doors left open because the offices get too hot, making it difficult to concentrate.

The surroundings aren’t great either, with large garbage and recycling containers directly in front of the building — not ideal when bringing clients.

They have also recently refurbished parts of the building, but some of the design choices are questionable. One entire floor is bright red, which feels particularly unsuitable for a professional workspace.

Overall, the facilities, service and environment don’t justify the price. I would definitely compare other options before committing.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our experience at this funeral home was very negative due to the lack of tact and professionalism of the staff, with the exception of the first employee who assisted us on our first day. He helped us choose everything with great empathy and respect, and was a 10 out of 10 both personally and professionally.

We also want to highlight that the farewell ceremony in the chapel was very beautiful. They made it very personal, intimate, and pleasant within such a painful situation. The decorations, the music, and the ambiance were all very well thought out, and we really appreciated that.

However, the treatment from the rest of the staff was very different.

During the wake, we had a problem with the flowers, and one of the employees came in talking loudly and saying, "So, what's wrong with the flowers?" We find it completely inappropriate to address such a problem in the middle of a wake and in front of the family.

The worst part was the lack of privacy when it came time to say goodbye. When we wanted to spend a few quiet minutes by the coffin, the worker remained there, holding the lid and making gestures as if to close it, while glancing at his watch. We felt watched and constantly pressured to hurry, unable to say our goodbyes properly.

Furthermore, during our visit, they offered the family no kindness whatsoever, not even a simple bottle of water.

I believe that in a funeral service, humane treatment, empathy, discretion, and respect should be paramount.

When I went to pick it up, they gave me a repair receipt. I explained what they told me when I dropped it off, and they bluntly told me they weren't going to discuss it with me. I explained that I was traveling from out of town and it wasn't worth going back another day, but they didn't care. In the end, I paid and took my chain. I will never go to or buy anything else at this jewelry store.

one_star_reviews.text: My experience with Maite was absolutely dreadful and corroborates what another review describes. From the beginning, she exuded a constant sense of urgency, constantly checking her watch and making the patient uncomfortable. In addition to her approach during sessions, the worst part came when I expressed how I felt: far from welcoming me with humility, professionalism, or empathy, she reacted with appalling ego and wanted to dismiss me in five minutes. With a moral depravity unbecoming of someone working in mental health, she arrogantly told me that the problem was mine. Seeing other people's experiences, it's clear that the problem isn't the patient's, but rather her complete lack of ethics and human tact. To say something like that to a patient speaks volumes about her character; it's a moral depravity that is frightening. I absolutely do not recommend her.

Terrible service. Some time ago, my daughter had the timing belt changed there, and it broke before the required time or mileage had been reached. I spoke with a guy named David, who did the work, and he told me to bring the car and the parts in to file a claim. When I arrived, I was shocked by the awful treatment. He questioned everything: whether we had mistreated the car, whether the belt had actually been changed (I had the receipt), and whether the parts were no longer covered under warranty (to which I asked him why he'd made me come in then). When I had the problem fixed elsewhere and showed him the receipt, he made comments like, "How do I know you paid for it?" (I also had proof of payment, although I don't think it was necessary to claim the warranty on the parts or, failing that, the installation they did). Anyway, don't let any repairs go wrong there, because in addition to them refusing to process the claim after making me go there, I had to endure one disrespectful act after another. Days later, he told me via WhatsApp that there was nothing to be done... just like that. I was going to talk to the brand, to the mechanic who did the repair, to everyone... he did nothing and threw the parts away.
The whole thing cost me €900 and not even an apology.

one_star_reviews.text: Discrimination by the owner of the Maria Cristina Civic Center campus against my 11-year-old son because of his disability. I waited a few weeks to see if there would be any empathy, but given the woman's behavior, I think a review is better than a lawsuit. I've been taking my son to the English camp at the civic center for a month, organized by this company. My son has Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and ADHD. The first week he goes to the camp and is generally fine, but the following week new children arrive. My son has clashes with some of them, and this woman called me on Wednesday. There's only one monitor for 12 or 15 children, who has to keep an eye on your son and can't attend to the others. The director of the civic centers called me, scared. We're afraid my 11-year-old son might do something dangerous, like kill someone. I asked her, "Do you want me to take him out?" She said yes, but that's not possible. This is at a community center (it's for everyone, right?). Then, to top it all off, I pay €190 for one month of camp; the price varies depending on whether you go for 1, 2, 3, or 4 weeks. I ask for a partial refund of the €190 for one month. They refund me €70 and charge me as if I had booked two weeks/€120/of camp (plus, I didn't even go on Thursday and Friday of one of those weeks because they asked me to leave). Then the real absurdity came when their WhatsApp status shows a picture of the Palestinian flag with a tree growing. It comes from the heart; I support the Palestinian cause from 4,000 km away from my sofa, but 300 meters away they discriminate against an 11-year-old boy because of his special needs. The level of behavior is so low that I can hardly say more.

The repair cost me almost more than the tire itself. I explained the problem to them by email, and they ignored me and didn't even reply... Well, that's all I have to say. They know I won't be buying from them again, that's for sure.

one_star_reviews.text:
Beware of this center!

My experience with this center has been very disappointing. I went there myself this past winter, and after several sessions, I decided to stop because I felt the therapy wasn't progressing: they listened to me, but I wasn't receiving any tools or seeing any real intervention. I thought perhaps I simply hadn't clicked with the therapist.

Months later, we took our teenage son for a serious problem, and with a different therapist, we had practically the same experience. When we asked why they weren't working on the problem yet, the therapist herself told us that she was building a relationship with him. I can understand that at first, but weeks went by, and we still saw no progress or tools.

My insurance covers 10 sessions, and in my case, there's a co-payment. After that, if you want to continue, you have to do it privately. Honestly, after going through this twice, we're left with the feeling that the insurance sessions are used up while building a relationship, and that by the time they end, the patient is already too involved to start over with another professional.

I can't say for sure that it's a deliberate strategy, but as patients, that's the feeling we got. And considering it involves the emotional well-being of a child, I find it especially worrying.

Based on our experience, we won't be returning.

one_star_reviews.text:
Completely dissatisfied, and it's a shame I can't give it zero stars. To begin with, when I walked in and said good morning, no one responded. 🙂
This time, I brought six different documents to be printed, including one for Social Security. They handed them to me mixed up and unorganized. I believe the least a stationery store can do is offer the option to staple or separate them; if staples cost money, they should charge for them, but you shouldn't hand out six mixed-up documents on the counter and leave the customer to sort it out.

Furthermore, one of the documents came out tiny. I admit the initial mistake was mine in sending it like that, but if it's clearly visible on the computer screen that the size is unsuitable, the professional thing to do would be to inform the customer and ask if they want to modify it, even if it incurs an additional cost.

When I mentioned it, instead of admitting the error, they insisted they had printed them "exactly as I had sent them." Their manner was also unpleasant.

On another occasion, I asked for a small piece of tape, and he told me he sold it. I told him to sell me one then, and he replied, "Well, this time it's free."

I always treat those who work with the public with respect, and I expect the same in return. It's a shame, because I keep coming back precisely because I want to support local businesses, but these experiences make me consider not returning.

one_star_reviews.text: I'm giving it one star so I can share my experience. I bought paint for my house's facade, pre-mixed at the store, and asked the saleswoman if I'd have any problem getting more paint made if needed. She assured me it wouldn't be a problem, that the paint would turn out exactly the same. A year later, I returned with the paint's reference number and color, and asked the saleswoman if they could make the same color using that reference number. She assured me it would be the same, and she said yes. They made me 4 liters, and the color was completely different from the one I had previously bought. I used it on my house, and a month ago, I returned with the same reference number to get the same paint made, which they had guaranteed would turn out exactly the same. To my surprise, the saleswoman told me they couldn't make it because they didn't have the colorants. I asked when the colorants would arrive, and she replied that they hadn't ordered them and that she didn't know if they were in stock at the factory. Seeing her lack of interest in identifying the dyes and providing a solution, I decided to leave the store, quite dissatisfied and annoyed with the saleswoman's behavior. Luckily, another paint store offered me a satisfactory solution.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had previously left a very positive review of this workshop, but I felt compelled to change it. Firstly, they gave me an inflated quote to repair a 1990 GS500E that had been sitting for 10 years. After 3-4 months in the workshop and riding it (though not much, as I always returned to the workshop after a few days), I decided to go to another workshop to ask about it. Upon arrival, they demonstrated that the motorcycle was running poorly in about 5 seconds, specifically on one cylinder.

After inspecting the motorcycle, they discovered fuel leaks that they failed to repair, despite the strong smell of gasoline and the obvious leak. The front tire, which they included in their estimate, was inflated to 1.6 bar when it should have been between 2 and 2.5 bar, and the rear tire was completely flat. I had to replace the fuel tank because the original one was rusted and pitted, and I had to find a used one myself, because anyone who knows about these bikes knows that parts are scarce, and they didn't offer me the option of finding a suitable replacement. A few weeks later, a coworker wanted to take an older Suzuki (newer than mine) to this same shop, and based on their experience with my bike, they told him they don't work on older motorcycles. In short, considering the money and time invested, plus the results, I don't recommend this shop for any repairs or maintenance other than routine work.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience and the result of my breast lift.

I paid for this surgery expecting a professional result, but I have been left deeply unhappy with the outcome. My nipples are positioned far too high, they are uneven, and they can be visible above certain bras and clothing. I am also unhappy with the appearance of the scars and have experienced ongoing discomfort.

On top of this, not all of the stitches around my nipples were properly removed. I have been left with what appear to be retained stitches under the skin, which are now visible as black dots around the nipple area. Months after surgery, I should not be dealing with something like this.

What has made the situation even worse is the way my concerns have been handled afterwards. When I raised these issues, I did not feel that my concerns were taken seriously. Instead of taking responsibility or offering me a satisfactory solution, I felt that the result was being blamed on my own breasts/body.

I trusted this surgeon with my body, paid a significant amount of money, and now I am seeking an independent medical opinion and considering making a formal complaint through the appropriate authorities in Spain.

I personally would not choose to have another procedure here. Based on my own experience, I strongly recommend that anyone considering surgery carefully research their surgeon, ask to see long-term results, and understand what options they have if they are unhappy with the outcome.

one_star_reviews.text:
I requested my medical records because I needed them for a personal matter, and the doctor's response seemed completely disproportionate to a request of this nature.

He told me that requesting them was "very serious," that it implied "distrust of your doctor," and, what surprised me most, that if I decided to request them, "from that moment on, you'll have to find another doctor."

At no point was I questioning his work or showing distrust. I simply wanted access to my own medical records, and I had previously explained the reason for my request.

I perfectly understand that there is a procedure, that it has to be requested in writing, or that it might take some time. What I consider inappropriate was the way he responded, associating a legitimate request with a lack of trust and making the continuation of my medical care conditional on me not requesting my records.

Personally, I felt that he went too far in his response and that it was unnecessarily hostile and lacking in empathy. I believe that a situation like this could have been handled in a much more professional, respectful, and reassuring way for the patient.
